objective: The labor kernel answers §13's six readings plus its measurements, its next questions and the ones it declined — and a person can reach none of it. `GET /api/projects/:id/labor` is mounted, guarded and complete; `services/labor/view.ts` composes the whole answer; and there is no screen anywhere in the product, so the only way to read who produces this company's work is `npm run report:labor` on a terminal. §29's first sentence is that a product is what a person can do, and the one question this kernel exists to answer — which of the things we do still needs a person, and why — is today answerable only by somebody with shell access. Every other kernel that a person is meant to read has a surface: the manufacturing programme has `/machines`, Cash has `/cash`, the register has `/register`. Labor has none.
expectedOutcome: A project member opens a Labor destination in the Russell shell and reads what the server already answers: how many workflows and tasks there are, the tasks that still depend on a person and which of the six reasons makes each necessary, the automation frontier with each task's blockers and their remedies, the bottlenecks, the capacity needs, the role-compression history in both directions, the per-workflow economics, every measurement with its evidence class, the question Brain would ask next with its recorded reason, and the ones it declined with theirs. Every sentence on the screen is one the server composed. A reader who cannot see the project gets the same refusal every other project-scoped screen gives.
nonGoals: Composing any sentence in the client. `Machines.tsx` is the precedent and its rule is the rule: the screen renders the service's own verdict and composes none of its own, because a screen that paraphrases a verdict eventually paraphrases it wrongly.

Adding any control that writes. This is a reading. Declaring a workflow, assigning a task and recording a human necessity are decisions with their own routes, their own levels and their own guards, and none of them belongs in this change.

Inventing a figure. §11's four measurements are UNKNOWN on this Brain and must render as UNKNOWN with the thing that would measure them named — never as zero, never as a percentage, and never omitted because a blank looks untidy.
Deriving anything the server already derives. No second reading of the same rows in TypeScript; if a number is wanted and the payload does not carry it, the payload is where it is added.
Touching `services/labor/`, the routes, the policy module or any schema. The server side of this is finished.
Any authorization decision in the client. A screen is not a guard, and `requirePerson` plus `requireProject` already decide who may read this.

acceptanceConditions.statement: A Labor destination exists in the Russell shell, reachable the way `/machines` is reachable, and renders every one of the twelve fields `LaborView` carries — including the empty ones, which say what is true rather than disappearing.

Every human-readable string on the screen that states a finding, a reason, a blocker, a remedy or a verdict comes from the payload. A test reads the rendered document against a payload and fails if the component introduces one of its own.
A measurement whose evidence class is UNKNOWN renders as unknown, beside the thing that would measure it, and no branch of the component can turn it into a number or a percentage.

Loading, empty, forbidden and error are four different screens, and the forbidden one does not claim the work is absent — §24's rule, because the server cannot distinguish absent from forbidden and the last hop must not invent an answer either.

A re-read leaves the previous answer up until the new one arrives, so nothing a person is part-way through reading is unmounted by a refresh — the defect §29 and §39 both record, once at People and once at Machines.
The screen obeys `tests/step12bResponsive.test.tsx`: it reflows by container rather than viewport, carries no `min-width` wider than a phone, and nothing on it is taken off the page at any width.
At least one new assertion is run against a neutered version of the guard it covers, and the commit says which one and what it failed with.

rollbackRequirement: Discard the branch. Nothing on the server moves, no schema changes, no route is added or altered, and no existing screen's behaviour depends on this one.
